post_hoist_selection.rationale: The 23 evaluator Dockerfiles repeatedly rewrite their owner START/END tags after adding go:build ignore directives, commenting test bodies, copying compatibility source, replacing go.mod/go.sum, and running go get or go mod tidy. Those mutations are endpoint-local test suppression or dependency drift, not a common runtime operation. For every runnable ref with evidence, retain the strict cross-SIF majority tree and drop owner-only mutations. A tie or lack of a strict majority remains blocking.

retained: offline Go module cache assembled from the evaluator SIFs
excluded_from_common_environment: endpoint-specific go get and go mod tidy tree changes

canonical_fallback_rule: Only a CSV-only milestone with no runnable ref in any evaluator may use canonical objects. Treat the declared commits as a partial order rather than trusting CSV order: require exactly one minimal declared commit, exactly one maximal declared commit, every declared commit reachable from the minimum and able to reach the maximum, and exactly one parent for the minimum. START is that parent and END is the unique maximum. M002 ends at 130e1ba, M012 ends at 1ebbc6f, and M016 ends at 9da76fb; this explicitly avoids pretending their CSV order is linear. The authority is recorded as canonical_no_runnable_evidence.
